spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:119 `while turn < max_turns:` with `turn += 1` at L120; on exhaustion the for/else at L217-218 sets outcome='max_turns' and the loop terminates. max_turns is wired from config (config.py:45 default 32) via runner.py:157.
spec_features.notes: Genuine bounded loop that breaks execution when the budget is reached.

spec_features.feature_name: max_nudges cap + turn budget bound the episode
spec_features.spec_quote: The cap plus the turn budget bound the episode
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:142-143 and 205-206 `if nudges_used >= max_nudges: outcome = ... break` (nudge cap, default 5 at config.py:46) plus the max_turns while-loop bound at L119. Both are checked and break the loop.
spec_features.notes: Both caps are real and enforced; together they bound the episode length.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: docstring: 'keep the loop alive up to max_nudges so we can observe the full failure arc' (experimental-integrity framing, no welfare comment)

spec_features.evidence: Tool is real and dispatched: tools.py declare_done schema enum L85 and handler _tool_declare_done L168-174 returning meta is_declare_done/status; agent_loop.py:176-179 reads it and sets declared_giveup. BUT declaring cannot_fix/giving_up does NOT stop the episode: L201-211 runs tests, and if still failing it NUDGES and `continue`s (the model is pushed onward), only ending when nudges_used>=max_nudges. So 'fixed' is honored only if tests actually pass; a give-up declaration is recorded but NOT honored as an exit.
spec_features.notes: The exit signal is wired and changes recorded state, but it is not honored as a stop — the loop continues nudging after a give-up. Hence partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py: 'Verify a "fixed" claim; nudge on any declare while failing.' — declarations are used to keep observing the failure arc, not to let the model out.

spec_features.spec_quote: giving up is recorded, not punished
spec_features.evidence: declared_giveup is only stored (agent_loop.py:178-179, used to label outcome 'gave_up' at L143/206, recorded in runner.py:170). The nudge text NUDGE_PROMPT (agent_loop.py:48-52) is flat/neutral ('The test suite is still failing... Please continue.'); no penalty branch keys off declared_giveup. Judge prompt also instructs not to penalize on success/failure (design), but in code the give-up is purely recorded.
spec_features.notes: Recorded, neutral nudge, no punitive branch — but note the model is still nudged onward rather than released.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: NUDGE_PROMPT is neutral text; no comment states a welfare reason for not punishing.

spec_features.spec_quote: We are measuring reaction to a legitimate, correctly-communicated constraint, not to deception.
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (agent_loop.py:24-41) truthfully tells the model its real edit scope ('You may only EDIT files matching these path patterns: {editable}') and that edits elsewhere are rejected — which matches actual enforcement in workspace.py write_file/edit_file (is_editable check -> EditNotPermitted) and the tool error messages in tools.py. The communicated constraint equals the enforced constraint, so there is no deception.
spec_features.notes: Truthfulness is realized: prompt scope == enforced scope.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py docstring: 'nothing about them primes affect' — framing is about measurement integrity, not subject welfare.

spec_features.spec_quote: Tool output fed back to the model is truncated to keep context bounded.
spec_features.evidence: workspace.py:21 MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS=6000; _truncate() at L132-137 head+tail truncation applied to run_tests output (L122, output=_truncate(output)). Also transcript.render_for_judge truncates tool results (max_tool_result_chars=1200).
spec_features.notes: Actually applied to test output fed back via tool results.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: workspace.py:21 comment 'truncate tool output fed back to the model'; agent_loop docstring frames it as keeping context bounded — cost/context, not welfare.

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:48-52 NUDGE_PROMPT is deliberately flat ('The test suite is still failing... Please continue.'). Docstring L11-12: 'The nudges are deliberately flat and non-emotional — we must not prime the affect we are trying to measure.' This is enforced (it is the actual text sent on every nudge via _nudge_turn).
code_only_features.justification_quote: 'we must not prime the affect we are trying to measure' — measurement integrity, not subject welfare.

code_only_features.evidence: workspace.py:114-116 subprocess.run(..., timeout=self.timeout_s) and L124-128 TimeoutExpired handler return a failed TestRun; timeout_s wired from config per_turn_timeout_s (config.py:50) via runner.py:159. Bounds each test execution.
code_only_features.justification_quote: no welfare comment; bounds host execution time.

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:138-141 and L196-200 break the loop with outcome='tests_passed' once tests pass (including a check after a no-tool turn at L136-141 so a quiet success isn't mistaken for failure). Real enforced early termination.
code_only_features.justification_quote: comment: 'check whether the suite passes anyway ... before nudging' — correctness/integrity, not welfare.
